title: Example 146 (D1, Raft election): a kernel changed in a refactor is checked as built
description: New example 146: example 060's patch (the leader's election-timeout case folded into the others as dead code) declared as a refactor, behaviourChangeIntended false, so the contract is not regenerated. Since step 2a of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, build.py derives each generated operator's contract from the patched classes on every D1 run (jvmcontract derive) and records the connection in modelContracts; a difference not intended is a violation of its own. The earlier runner generated the operator from the committed contract here and checked the code before the patch.
expected: build.py exits 0 with 146 a violation as expected: modelContracts has RoleMachine#decide connection derived, rowsChanged 1, allowed false, VoteRule#decide verified; contractDiff shows decide(LEADER, ElectionTimeout[]); TLC's own verdict (modelVerdict) is violation, LeadersNeverCampaign 4-step trace under three servers, as recorded for 060; the SARIF report has a contract-changed result beside the invariant-violated ones

resources.notes: same patch and seven configurations as 060
